uncited: This family implements the standard algorithm for determining the intersection interval $[t_{min}, t_{max}]$ between a ray and an Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) by computing intersections with the box's six defining planes (slabs).
It solves the fundamental problem of efficiently culling rays that miss a volume primitive or determining the precise entry and exit distances for ray marching.

It is distinguished from [Ray-Cube Intersection](2466-ray-cube-intersection.md) by returning scalar $t$-intervals rather than 3D coordinates and face indices, and from [AABB Intersection via Face Traversal](13498-aabb-intersection-via-face-traversal.md) by computing the full interval upfront rather than stepping through voxels.
The core mechanism relies on the "slab" concept: an AABB is the intersection of three orthogonal slabs, where each slab is the region between two parallel planes perpendicular to an axis.
where $b_i$ is either the min or max bound.
To avoid division by zero, the reciprocal direction $\mathbf{r}_i = 1/d_i$ is precomputed.
A ray intersects the AABB if $t_{min} \le t_{max}$ and the interval is valid (e.g., $t_{max} > t_{min} + \epsilon$).
This method is $O(1)$ and branchless when implemented with vector operations, making it suitable for GPU acceleration .
It is widely used in BVH traversal, voxel rendering, and collision detection due to its simplicity and efficiency.
